shared_facts.value: Granular research control requires three distinct primitives: starting research jobs, polling for status, and importing discovered sources [1].
The existing MCP research implementation is restricted to a high-level macro (notebooklm_workflow_research) which does not support staged or selective research behavior [1], [2].

fe_facts.value: The CLI initiates research via the 'add-research' command located in src/notebooklm/cli/source.py [1].
CLI provides status, wait, and import flows through src/notebooklm/cli/research.py [1].

be_facts.value: The underlying SDK (src/notebooklm/_research.py) exposes start(), poll(), and import_sources() methods [1].
No dedicated research tool module is registered in the current MCP server boundary; research is only reachable via the workflows module [3], [1].

claims.claim: Direct research controls are described as 'absent from MCP' [4].
Research has 'Partial MCP parity' because of the high-level macro [1].

contradictions.open_question: Does the conversion requirement mandate wrapping the existing macro or exposing the raw SDK primitives as new CLI-native entry points?

missing_info.summary: Specific CLI flags and argument structures for 'status', 'wait', and 'import' flows in src/notebooklm/cli/research.py are not detailed in the excerpts [1].

open_questions.summary: How to bridge the gap between high-level MCP workflow macros and raw SDK research primitives [5].

Will the CLI implementation for the research-pipeline-controller continue to use the source.py entry point for initiation, or will all research-related controls be unified under a single research CLI module [1]?
